cards.name: Duotone
cards.summary: Converts a grayscale image to Duotone mode: the gray values are printed with one to four inks (monotone, duotone, tritone, quadtone), each ink with its own curve, giving the rich tinted look of a two-colour print job. Only available on an 8-bit Grayscale document; it was greyed out in every RGB scratch state tried.
cards.how: Type: Monotone, Duotone, Tritone or Quadtone. For each ink pick a colour (usually a Pantone spot from Color Libraries) and edit its curve to control where in the tonal range it prints; Overprint Colors previews how the inks mix. Presets ship for common black + spot pairs.
use_for: two-colour poster or flyer printed with black plus one Pantone spot
warm sepia or cool cyan-black toned photo for a brochure or book cover
matching a brand spot colour in a single-image print ad
avoid: a duotone look for screen only: a Gradient Map adjustment layer keeps the file RGB and editable
starting from an RGB or 16-bit image: convert to 8-bit Image > Mode > Grayscale first
cards.script_api: No confirmed script route. Candidate executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('convertMode'), desc, DialogModes.ALL) with desc: to (T) = class Duotone (DtnI) was tried live on the RGB scratch document and opened a dialog titled 'Adobe Photoshop' that does not name the command; on a Grayscale document it should open Duotone Options (unverified).

review.changes: script_api reworded to what the batch recorded (a dialog titled 'Adobe Photoshop', not a confirmed alert)

cards.name: Grayscale
cards.summary: Converts the document to Grayscale mode: the colour channels are replaced by one Gray channel, colour information is discarded and the working gray profile is assigned (observed: RGB sRGB -> Gray, Dot Gain 20%). The image looks like a plain black-and-white photo.
cards.how: In the UI a 'Discard color information?' alert appears (it points to Image > Adjustments > Black & White for more control); click Discard. No other settings.
use_for: one-colour newspaper or newsletter ad that must be a true single-channel black file
preparing a photo for Duotone or Bitmap mode (both need Grayscale first)
laser engraving or single-ink screen-print artwork
avoid: a black-and-white look you may want to tune or undo: use a Black & White adjustment layer and keep RGB
files headed for screen or colour print: the colour is gone for good once saved
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('convertMode'), desc, DialogModes.NO) with desc: to (T) = class Grayscale (Grys); verified live on a scratch RGB document (channels Red,Green,Blue -> Gray). DOM (used live as setup by this harvest): app.activeDocument.changeMode(ChangeMode.GRAYSCALE).

cards.name: Indexed Color
cards.summary: Converts the image to 8-bit Indexed Color: every pixel is mapped to a colour table of at most 256 colours, giving a flat, posterised or dithered look and a single Index channel. Layers are flattened.
cards.how: Palette: Exact, System (Mac/Windows), Web, Uniform, Local or Master Perceptual / Selective / Adaptive, Custom or Previous; Colors sets how many entries; Forced adds black and white, primaries or web colours; Transparency and Matte handle transparent areas; Dither (None, Diffusion, Pattern, Noise) with Amount trades banding for grain. Image > Mode > Color Table edits the palette afterwards.
use_for: pixel-art or retro game sprite with a fixed small palette
limited-colour artwork for screen printing or embroidery separations
GIF-style banner with a controlled colour count
avoid: photos that need further editing: most filters and adjustments are unavailable in Indexed mode
just exporting a small GIF or PNG-8: File > Export > Save for Web (Legacy) indexes on export and keeps the master RGB
cards.script_api: var o = new IndexedConversionOptions(); o.palette = Palette.LOCALADAPTIVE; o.colors = 16; o.forced = ForcedColors.NONE; o.transparency = false; app.activeDocument.changeMode(ChangeMode.INDEXEDCOLOR, o); verified live (channels Red,Green,Blue -> Index).

cards.name: Lab Color
cards.summary: Converts the document to Lab Color mode: the image is split into a Lightness channel and two colour channels (a = green-magenta, b = blue-yellow), device-independent so no ICC profile is kept. The picture looks the same; only the channel structure changes.
cards.how: No dialog. Work in the Channels panel: edit Lightness alone for tone and sharpening, or steepen a and b curves for stronger colour, then convert back to RGB or CMYK.
use_for: sharpening or denoising only the Lightness channel of a product or portrait photo so colours do not halo
the 'Lab colour boost': steepening the a and b curves for punchy travel or food photos
a neutral in-between space when moving a file between very different RGB and CMYK profiles
avoid: final delivery files: web, print and most apps expect RGB or CMYK
repeated back-and-forth conversions: each one rounds values and can band smooth gradients
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('convertMode'), desc, DialogModes.NO) with desc: to (T) = class Lab color (LbCM); verified live on a scratch RGB document (channels Red,Green,Blue -> Lightness,a,b; profile dropped). DOM alternative (unverified): app.activeDocument.changeMode(ChangeMode.LAB).

cards.name: Multichannel
cards.summary: Converts the document to Multichannel mode: each channel becomes an independent 256-level grayscale channel with no colour model tying them together (observed: an RGB file became Cyan, Magenta and Yellow channels and lost its profile). Composite colour preview changes accordingly; layers are not supported.
cards.how: No dialog. Afterwards rename, recolour (Channel Options: ink colour and solidity) or delete channels in the Channels panel to build custom-ink separations.
use_for: building custom spot-ink separations for screen printing or specialty packaging
turning a CMYK file into separate plate channels to edit or drop one ink
preparing a DCS 2.0 file for a spot-colour print workflow
avoid: ordinary photo or layout work: the layers are flattened and most adjustments and filters stop working
adding one spot colour to a normal file: add a Spot Channel from the Channels panel instead

DOM alternative (unverified): app.activeDocument.changeMode(ChangeMode.MULTICHANNEL).

cards.name: RGB Color
cards.summary: Converts the document to RGB Color mode using the working RGB space (observed: Grayscale Dot Gain 20% -> RGB sRGB IEC61966-2.1). A grayscale image still looks gray but now has Red, Green and Blue channels and can take colour.
cards.how: No dialog for a plain conversion; to land in a specific RGB space use Edit > Convert to Profile instead.
use_for: colourising or tinting a black-and-white photo for a poster or social post
unlocking filters and adjustments that only run in RGB (many Filter Gallery and Neural Filters)
preparing a CMYK or grayscale asset for web and screen use
avoid: choosing the destination profile (Display P3, Adobe RGB): use Edit > Convert to Profile
expecting colour back after Grayscale: discarded colour is not restored, only the channels are

cards.name: Reveal All
cards.summary: Enlarges the canvas just enough to show every pixel of every layer that hangs outside it (observed: a layer moved 300 px to the right grew the canvas from 400x300 to 500x300). Layers keep their content; on a Background layer the added area takes the background colour.
use_for: recovering parts of a layer that were dragged or scaled off the edge of a banner or poster
growing the canvas to fit a pasted image larger than the document
avoid: setting an exact canvas size or anchor: use Image > Canvas Size
removing empty borders: use Image > Trim
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('revealAll'), new ActionDescriptor(), DialogModes.NO); verified live (size 400x300 -> 500x300). DOM alternative (unverified): app.activeDocument.revealAll().

cards.name: Trap
cards.summary: Applies trapping to a CMYK document: lighter colours are spread slightly under darker neighbours (by the set width) so thin white gaps do not appear if the printing plates misregister. The change is a few pixels at colour edges and is barely visible on screen. Needs a CMYK document (greyed out in every RGB state); observed live, it flattened the layers into the Background.
cards.how: Width: the trap distance, in pixels, points or millimetres; ask the print shop for the value (often a fraction of a point).
use_for: a CMYK flyer, label or packaging file with solid colours butting against each other, when the printer asks for trapping in the file
avoid: photos and continuous-tone images: trapping is for flat colour edges
most modern jobs: printers and RIPs usually trap at output, so ask before applying it yourself
layered masters: it flattens, so trap a copy
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('trap'), desc, DialogModes.NO) with desc: Width (Wdth) = 2 (unit #Pxl); verified live on a CMYK scratch document (history state 'Trap'). DOM alternative (unverified): app.activeDocument.trap(2).

cards.name: Trim
cards.summary: Crops the canvas down to the content by cutting away border areas that are transparent or that match a corner pixel's colour (observed: a 160x160 shape on a transparent 400x300 canvas trimmed to 160x160).
cards.how: Based On: Transparent Pixels, Top Left Pixel Color or Bottom Right Pixel Color; Trim Away: tick Top, Bottom, Left and Right to choose which sides are cut.
use_for: trimming a cut-out product, logo or icon PNG to its edges before export
removing a flat white or solid-colour border from a scanned or exported image
making sticker or emoji assets that sit tight to their artwork
avoid: keeping a uniform margin: Trim leaves none, so add padding with Image > Canvas Size afterwards
anti-aliased or noisy borders: near-matching pixels are kept, so the crop may stop short
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('trim'), desc, DialogModes.NO) with desc: trimBasedOn = enum trimBasedOn 'transparency', Top / Btom / Left / Rght = true; verified live (400x300 -> 160x160). DOM alternative (unverified): app.activeDocument.trim(TrimType.TRANSPARENT, true, true, true, true).

cards.name: Data Sets
cards.summary: Opens the Variables dialog on its Data Sets page, where named sets of values for the document's variables (text replacement, pixel replacement, visibility) are created, edited or imported from a text or CSV file, and previewed on the canvas. Greyed out in every scratch state: it needs variables defined first with Image > Variables > Define.
cards.how: Pick a data set from the list, step through sets with the arrows to preview, and edit each variable's value below; Import loads a comma- or tab-delimited file whose columns are the variable names. Output the results with File > Export > Data Sets as Files.
use_for: batch name badges, certificates or event passes from a spreadsheet of names and photos
product cards or social posts in many variants from one template
localised banner sets where only the headline text changes
avoid: documents with no variables defined: define them first with Image > Variables > Define
complex per-variant layout changes: script the document instead
cards.script_api: No script route harvested (no menuItemType or event label matches; 7803 is a menuBarInfo command id, and the harvest audit found runMenuItem refuses those ids). cards.name: Define
cards.summary: Opens the Variables dialog on its Define page, where the selected layer is turned into a data-driven variable: Visibility (show or hide), Pixel Replacement (swap the image from a file) or Text Replacement (swap a text layer's string), each with a name used by data sets.
cards.how: Choose the Layer, tick the variable types it should carry and name them. Pixel Replacement adds Method (Fit, Fill, As Is, Conform), an alignment point and Clip to Bounding Box. Then switch to Data Sets to enter or import values.
use_for: setting up a template for batch certificates, ID cards or price tags
turning a social-post design into a template whose headline and photo change per row of a spreadsheet
avoid: one-off edits: just edit the layer
variable data in vector layouts: Illustrator's Variables panel or CorelDRAW Print Merge suit those better

cards.name: Bottom Edges
cards.summary: Aligns the bottom edges of the selected layers to the lowest bottom edge among the selected layers. With an active selection it aligns the layers to the bottom of the selection instead. Needs two or more layers selected, or one layer plus a selection.
use_for: ground line of a product row or the baseline of a row of icons
snapping a single layer to a marquee selection (select an area, then align)
avoid: aligning to the canvas: Select > All first, then align (the layers snap to the full-canvas selection)
equal spacing between three or more layers: use Layer > Distribute
a locked layer or the Background: they do not move

cards.name: Bring Forward
cards.summary: Moves the selected layer one step up the stack, in front of the layer directly above it (inside its group). The harvest saw it greyed out in every scratch state (the active layer was already on top) and verified it live after selecting a lower layer; it is greyed out when the layer is already at the top of its stack.
use_for: nudging a text or logo layer above a photo or shape it is hidden behind
fine-tuning overlap order in a collage or poster comp
avoid: moving a layer to the very top: use Bring to Front
the Background layer: it cannot be reordered until converted to a normal layer

cards.name: Bring to Front

The harvest saw it greyed out in every scratch state (the active layer was already on top) and verified it live after selecting a lower layer; it is greyed out when the layer is already on top.
use_for: putting a headline, logo or call-to-action button above all imagery in a banner
bringing a watermark or frame layer to the very front
avoid: moving it out of its group: drag it in the Layers panel instead

cards.name: Create Clipping Mask
cards.summary: Clips the selected layer to the layer directly below it: the upper layer shows only inside the pixels (or shape, or text) of the base layer, and is indented with a down arrow in the Layers panel. Non-destructive; Release Clipping Mask undoes it.
use_for: filling headline text with a photo or texture for a poster or thumbnail
confining an adjustment layer to one cut-out product so the background is untouched
placing a photo inside a shape frame on a social template
avoid: hiding parts of a layer by painting: use a layer mask
the bottom layer of a stack or the Background: there is nothing below to clip to
cards.script_api: executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('groupEvent'), desc, DialogModes.NO) with desc: null = reference to the target layer (Lyr); verified live (layer became clipped). DOM alternative (unverified): app.activeDocument.activeLayer.grouped = true.

cards.name: Hidden Layers
cards.summary: Deletes every hidden layer (eye turned off) in the document in one go, after a confirmation alert. Greyed out when the document has no hidden layers, as in every scratch state tried.
cards.how: A confirmation alert asks before deleting; there are no other settings.
use_for: cleaning a layered comp of discarded alternatives before handing it to a client or printer
shrinking a PSD template's file size before sharing
avoid: keeping alternative versions for later: use Layer Comps or save a copy first
deleting only some hidden layers: select and delete them in the Layers panel
